text: 常记溪亭日暮，沉醉不知归路
pinyin: cháng jì xī tíng rì mù, chén zuì bù zhī guī lù
literal: often · remember · stream · pavilion · sun · set, deeply · drunk · not · know · return · way
natural: I often recall the stream pavilion at dusk, so drunk I lost the way home

meaning.en: The opening of Li Qingzhao's early lyric: a carefree evening of boating and wine so absorbing that she forgot the way back.
meaning.zh: 李清照早期词作的开头：回忆溪亭游玩、酒醉忘归的畅快傍晚。

equivalents: lost in the joy of the moment
so happy I forgot the way home

examples.zh: 朋友聚会后回想起来，不禁感叹“常记溪亭日暮，沉醉不知归路”。
examples.en: Looking back on the get-together, she could not help quoting 'I often recall the stream pavilion at dusk, so drunk I lost the way home'.

examples.zh: 那个傍晚的湖边小酌，真有“常记溪亭日暮，沉醉不知归路”的味道。
examples.en: That evening's drinks by the lake really had the feel of 'so drunk I lost the way home'.

story.en: Li Qingzhao (c. 1084-c. 1155) wrote this short lyric to the tune 如梦令 about a day of boating on a lake and drinking until dusk.
story.zh: 李清照（约1084—约1155）所作小令《如梦令》，写溪亭泛舟、饮酒至日暮的游兴。

usage.en: Quoted when recalling a happy, carefree outing. Literary; the poem goes on to the famous 争渡，争渡，惊起一滩鸥鹭.
usage.zh: 回忆愉快惬意的出游时引用，书面语。词中接着是“争渡，争渡，惊起一滩鸥鹭”。

text: 莫笑农家腊酒浑，丰年留客足鸡豚
pinyin: mò xiào nóng jiā là jiǔ hún, fēng nián liú kè zú jī tún
literal: do not · laugh · farm · family · winter · wine · cloudy, bumper · year · keep · guest · plenty · chicken · pork
natural: do not mock the farmers' cloudy winter wine: in a good year there is plenty of chicken and pork for guests

meaning.en: Lu You's picture of village hospitality: the homemade wine may be cloudy, but in a good harvest year the hosts are generous.
meaning.zh: 陆游笔下的农家待客之情：自酿的腊酒虽然浑浊，但丰收之年，酒菜十分丰盛。

examples.zh: 农家乐的老板笑着说：“莫笑农家腊酒浑，丰年留客足鸡豚。”
examples.en: The owner of the farmhouse restaurant smiled and said, 'Do not mock our cloudy wine; in a good year there is plenty for guests.'

examples.zh: 到乡下做客，主人家摆满土菜，真是莫笑农家腊酒浑，丰年留客足鸡豚。
examples.en: Visiting the countryside, the host spread out home-style dishes: 'do not mock the cloudy wine, in a good year there is plenty for guests'.

story.en: Lu You (1125-1210) wrote 《游山西村》 in 1167 while living in retirement in his home village, Shanyin; it also contains 山重水复疑无路，柳暗花明又一村.
story.zh: 陆游（1125—1210）于1167年闲居家乡山阴时作《游山西村》，诗中另有“山重水复疑无路，柳暗花明又一村”。

usage.en: Quoted for warm, simple rural hospitality and often seen on farmhouse-restaurant signs. Literary but widely known.
usage.zh: 形容农村淳朴热情的待客之道，农家乐招牌上常见，书面语但流传很广。

text: 遗民泪尽胡尘里，南望王师又一年
pinyin: yí mín lèi jìn hú chén lǐ, nán wàng wáng shī yòu yī nián
literal: left-behind · people · tears · run dry · barbarian · dust · in, south · gaze · royal · army · again · one · year
natural: the abandoned people have wept dry in the barbarian dust, gazing south for the royal army another year

meaning.en: Lu You on the Song subjects living under Jin rule: they have cried until no tears are left, and each year still look south in vain for the army to come.
meaning.zh: 陆游写沦陷区的宋朝遗民：泪已流尽，年复一年向南盼望朝廷军队，却始终落空。

equivalents: waiting year after year for rescue that never comes

examples.zh: 读到“遗民泪尽胡尘里，南望王师又一年”，老师讲起了南宋的偏安。
examples.en: On reading 'the abandoned people have wept dry, gazing south for the army another year', the teacher spoke of the Southern Song's retreat south.

examples.zh: 他把等了多年的消息比作“遗民泪尽胡尘里，南望王师又一年”，满是无奈。
examples.en: He compared his years of waiting for news to 'the abandoned people have wept dry, gazing south for the army another year', full of helplessness.

origin.source: 陆游《秋夜将晓出篱门迎凉有感二首》其二

story.en: Lu You wrote this poem in 1192 in his village home; the Jin held the Central Plains, and the whole poem laments that the old northern lands were still unrecovered.
story.zh: 陆游1192年居乡时作此诗，当时中原仍被金占据，全诗感叹故土未复。

usage.en: Quoted for patriotic grief or for long, unrewarded waiting. Literary. 胡尘 refers to the Jurchen-ruled north.
usage.zh: 用于表达爱国忧思，或比喻久盼无果的等待，书面语。“胡尘”指金人统治下的北方。

text: 早岁那知世事艰，中原北望气如山
pinyin: zǎo suì nǎ zhī shì shì jiān, zhōng yuán běi wàng qì rú shān
literal: early · years · how · know · world · affairs · hard, Central · Plains · north · gaze · spirit · like · mountain
natural: in my youth how could I know the world's hardships? Gazing north to the Central Plains, my spirit was like a mountain

meaning.en: Lu You looks back at his youthful confidence: he had no idea how hard life would be, and his spirit rose like a mountain when he looked towards the lost north.
meaning.zh: 陆游回顾年轻时的豪情：那时不知世事艰难，北望中原，气概如山。

equivalents: we were young and did not know how hard things would be

examples.zh: 回首创业之初，他感慨“早岁那知世事艰，中原北望气如山”。
examples.en: Looking back on the start of his business, he sighed, 'in my youth how could I know the world's hardships'.

examples.zh: 老教授引用“早岁那知世事艰，中原北望气如山”，提醒新生不要把前路想得太轻松。
examples.en: The old professor quoted 'in my youth how could I know the world's hardships, gazing north my spirit was like a mountain' to warn freshmen not to take the road ahead too lightly.

story.en: Lu You wrote 《书愤》 ('Venting Indignation') in 1186 at the age of sixty-one, after being out of office for years.
story.zh: 陆游1186年六十一岁、闲居多年后作《书愤》。

usage.en: Often quoted, especially the first half, for youthful naivety and ambition seen from later years. Literary.
usage.zh: 常引用（尤其上半句），表达年轻时不知世事艰难、胸怀壮志的心情，书面语。

text: 楼船夜雪瓜洲渡，铁马秋风大散关
pinyin: lóu chuán yè xuě guā zhōu dù, tiě mǎ qiū fēng dà sàn guān
literal: tower · ship · night · snow · Guazhou · ferry, iron · horse · autumn · wind · Dasan · Pass
natural: tower-ships in the night snow at Guazhou ferry, armoured horses in the autumn wind at Dasan Pass

meaning.en: Two remembered battle scenes from Lu You's younger days, one on the Yangtze and one on the northwestern frontier, set against his present, ageing self.
meaning.zh: 陆游回忆当年两处战场：长江边的瓜洲渡与西北边塞的大散关，对照今日的年迈闲居。

examples.zh: 爷爷讲起当年的战斗，仿佛又回到“楼船夜雪瓜洲渡，铁马秋风大散关”的岁月。
examples.en: Grandfather spoke of the battles of old as if back in the days of 'tower-ships in the night snow at Guazhou, armoured horses in the autumn wind at Dasan Pass'.

examples.zh: 影片结尾引用“楼船夜雪瓜洲渡，铁马秋风大散关”，勾起观众的豪迈之情。
examples.en: The film's ending quoted 'tower-ships in the night snow at Guazhou ...', stirring the audience's martial pride.

story.en: In 《书愤》 Lu You recalls campaigns at Guazhou on the Yangtze and the Dasan Pass in Shaanxi, where he had served in the 1170s.
story.zh: 陆游在《书愤》中追忆长江畔的瓜洲渡和陕西的大散关，1170年代他曾在西北任职。

usage.en: Quoted for martial memories and heroic scenes. Literary. A classic parallel couplet.
usage.zh: 用于追忆军旅往事或渲染豪迈战场，书面语，是有名的对偶句。

text: 此去经年，应是良辰好景虚设
pinyin: cǐ qù jīng nián, yīng shì liáng chén hǎo jǐng xū shè
literal: this · go · pass · year, surely · be · fine · hour · good · scene · empty · set
natural: after this parting, years will pass, and every fine hour and lovely scene will be wasted

meaning.en: From Liu Yong's farewell lyric: once we part, years will go by and even the most beautiful days and scenery will mean nothing without you.
meaning.zh: 柳永离别词中的名句：这一别要经年累月，再美的时光与景色也都形同虚设。

equivalents: without you, even paradise would be empty

examples.zh: 毕业典礼上，大家想起“此去经年，应是良辰好景虚设”，一时无言。
examples.en: At the graduation ceremony everyone recalled 'after this parting, every fine scene will be wasted', and fell silent.

examples.zh: 临行前的夜晚，他在卡片上抄下“此去经年，应是良辰好景虚设”。
examples.en: On the night before leaving, he copied 'after this parting, every fine hour will be wasted' on a card.

story.en: Liu Yong (c. 987-c. 1053) wrote this lyric about parting from a lover at the capital's outskirts; it is among the most famous farewell lyrics of the Song.
story.zh: 柳永（约987—约1053）此词写在汴京城外与恋人惜别，是宋词中最著名的送别之作之一。

usage.en: Quoted at partings between lovers or close friends. Literary and sentimental; it follows 多情自古伤离别，更那堪冷落清秋节.
usage.zh: 用于恋人、挚友离别，书面、伤感。词中上文是“多情自古伤离别，更那堪冷落清秋节”。

text: 靖康耻，犹未雪
pinyin: jìng kāng chǐ, yóu wèi xuě
literal: Jingkang · shame · still · not yet · washed away
natural: the shame of Jingkang has still not been washed away

meaning.en: A famous line from the middle of 'Man Jiang Hong' (after 莫等闲，白了少年头，空悲切): the humiliation of 1127, when the Jin captured the Song capital and two emperors, is still unavenged.
meaning.zh: 《满江红》中的名句：1127年金兵攻陷汴京、俘虏二帝的耻辱，至今尚未洗雪。

equivalents: the shame has yet to be wiped out

examples.zh: 这支球队输得太惨，队长在赛后说：“靖康耻，犹未雪。”
examples.en: The team lost badly, and after the match the captain said, 'The shame has yet to be wiped out.'

examples.zh: 史书记下了“靖康耻，犹未雪”的悲愤。
examples.en: The history books record the grief and anger of 'the shame of Jingkang has not yet been washed away'.

story.en: Traditionally attributed to Yue Fei (1103-1142); the 'Jingkang humiliation' was the fall of Kaifeng in 1127. Scholars debate whether the poem is really his.
story.zh: 传统上认为是岳飞（1103—1142）所作；“靖康耻”指1127年汴京陷落。学界对其是否岳飞所作有争议。

usage.en: Quoted for patriotic resolve or, jokingly, for a humiliating defeat one means to avenge. The attribution to Yue Fei is traditional but doubted by some scholars, since the poem is first recorded in the Ming.
usage.zh: 用于表达爱国决心，或半开玩笑地说要为惨败雪耻。传统上归于岳飞，但此词最早见于明代，部分学者对作者存疑。

text: 壮志饥餐胡虏肉，笑谈渴饮匈奴血
pinyin: zhuàng zhì jī cān hú lǔ ròu, xiào tán kě yǐn xiōng nú xuè
literal: grand · ambition · hungry · eat · barbarian · captive · flesh, laughing · talking · thirsty · drink · Xiongnu · blood
natural: with lofty resolve I would eat the flesh of the barbarians when hungry, and laughing and talking drink Xiongnu blood when thirsty

meaning.en: A fierce vow from 'Man Jiang Hong': an exaggerated image of burning hatred for the invaders and determination to defeat them.
meaning.zh: 《满江红》中的豪语，以夸张的比喻表达对侵略者的刻骨仇恨和杀敌的决心。

examples.zh: 课文讲到“壮志饥餐胡虏肉，笑谈渴饮匈奴血”，同学们读得慷慨激昂。
examples.en: When the text reached 'with lofty resolve I would eat the barbarians' flesh', the students read it with passion.

examples.zh: 这句“壮志饥餐胡虏肉，笑谈渴饮匈奴血”写出了英雄的满腔仇恨。
examples.en: The line shows the hero's burning hatred in full.

story.en: Part of 《满江红》, traditionally credited to Yue Fei; 胡虏 and 匈奴 are classical stock terms for northern foes, used here for the Jin.
story.zh: 出自传为岳飞所作的《满江红》；“胡虏”“匈奴”是古人对北方敌人的惯称，这里借指金人。

usage.en: A rhetorical, hyperbolic line from a patriotic poem. Today 胡虏 and 匈奴 are read as stock terms for historic enemies and the line is not applied to any present-day people. Attribution to Yue Fei is traditional but disputed.
usage.zh: 出自爱国词的夸张之语。今天“胡虏”“匈奴”只被看作历史上敌人的泛称，不指现实中的任何民族。作者归于岳飞是传统说法，但有争议。

text: 惶恐滩头说惶恐，零丁洋里叹零丁
pinyin: huáng kǒng tān tóu shuō huáng kǒng, líng dīng yáng lǐ tàn líng dīng
literal: Terror · Shoal · head · speak · fear, Lonely · Ocean · in · sigh · lonely
natural: at Terror Shoal I speak of terror, on the Lonely Ocean I sigh of loneliness

meaning.en: Wen Tianxiang plays on two place names: he names his fear at Huangkong Shoal and his solitary desolation on Lingding Ocean as his cause collapses.
meaning.zh: 文天祥巧用两个地名：在惶恐滩说惶恐，在零丁洋叹孤零，抒写国事败落的悲凉。

equivalents: fear and loneliness, in the very place names
alone and afraid at the end of the road

examples.zh: 读到“惶恐滩头说惶恐，零丁洋里叹零丁”，学生才注意到诗人对地名的巧用。
examples.en: On reaching 'at Terror Shoal I speak of terror', the students noticed the poet's clever use of place names.

examples.zh: 他把这几年的处境概括为“惶恐滩头说惶恐，零丁洋里叹零丁”。
examples.en: He summed up his last few years as 'terror at Terror Shoal, loneliness on the Lonely Ocean'.

story.en: Wen Tianxiang (1236-1283) wrote this poem in 1279 as a Yuan prisoner passing Lingding Ocean, refusing to urge the Song loyalists to surrender.
story.zh: 文天祥（1236—1283）于1279年被元军押解途经零丁洋时作此诗，拒绝写信招降宋军。

usage.en: A famous pair of puns on place names, usually followed by 人生自古谁无死，留取丹心照汗青. Literary.
usage.zh: 利用地名双关的名联，下句即“人生自古谁无死，留取丹心照汗青”，书面语。

text: 天地有正气，杂然赋流形
pinyin: tiān dì yǒu zhèng qì, zá rán fù liú xíng
literal: heaven · earth · have · upright · spirit, mixed · thus · endow · flowing · forms
natural: heaven and earth hold an upright spirit, which they bestow in many forms on all things

meaning.en: The opening of Wen Tianxiang's 'Song of Righteousness': a moral energy fills the universe and shows itself in rivers and mountains, and in upright people.
meaning.zh: 文天祥《正气歌》开篇：天地间有一种浩然正气，表现为山河，也体现在正直之人身上。

equivalents: the upright spirit of heaven and earth

examples.zh: 纪念馆的墙上写着“天地有正气，杂然赋流形”。
examples.en: On the wall of the memorial hall is written 'heaven and earth hold an upright spirit'.

examples.zh: 他在演讲开头引用“天地有正气，杂然赋流形”，赞扬见义勇为的市民。
examples.en: He opened his speech with 'heaven and earth hold an upright spirit' to praise the citizen who had stepped in to help.

story.en: Written in 1281 in a Yuan prison in Dadu (Beijing); the poem lists virtuous figures from history who held to their principles, and Wen was executed in 1283.
story.zh: 1281年文天祥被囚于元大都（今北京）狱中所作，诗中列举历史上坚守气节的人物；他于1283年就义。

usage.en: Quoted in praise of moral courage and integrity. Solemn and literary.
usage.zh: 用来赞扬气节与正义，庄重、书面。

text: 泉眼无声惜细流，树阴照水爱晴柔
pinyin: quán yǎn wú shēng xī xì liú, shù yīn zhào shuǐ ài qíng róu
literal: spring · eye · without · sound · cherish · thin · flow, tree · shade · reflect · water · love · clear · softness
natural: the spring is silent, as if cherishing its trickle; tree shade over the water loves the soft sunlight

meaning.en: The first couplet of Yang Wanli's 'Little Pond': a quiet spring and the shade of trees over a pond are described as if they cherish and love what they have.
meaning.zh: 杨万里《小池》的首联：无声的泉水珍惜着细细的水流，树荫映在水中，喜爱晴天的柔和。

equivalents: quiet beauty of a small pond

examples.zh: 语文课上，老师教我们背《小池》：“泉眼无声惜细流，树阴照水爱晴柔。”
examples.en: In Chinese class the teacher had us recite 'Little Pond': 'The spring is silent, cherishing its trickle ...'.

examples.zh: 公园里的小池塘，正是“泉眼无声惜细流，树阴照水爱晴柔”的样子。
examples.en: The little pond in the park is just as the poem says, 'the spring is silent, cherishing its trickle'.

story.en: Yang Wanli (1127-1206), a Southern Song poet known for fresh, lively nature verse, wrote 《小池》 as a four-line poem in early summer.
story.zh: 杨万里（1127—1206）是南宋诗人，以清新活泼的写景诗著称，《小池》是一首写初夏的七言绝句。

usage.en: A well-known children's poem couplet; the next lines are 小荷才露尖尖角，早有蜻蜓立上头. 树阴 is also written 树荫.
usage.zh: 儿童熟知的古诗开头，下接“小荷才露尖尖角，早有蜻蜓立上头”。“树阴”也写作“树荫”。

variants: 泉眼无声惜细流，树荫照水爱晴柔

text: 清风两袖朝天去，免得闾阎话短长
pinyin: qīng fēng liǎng xiù cháo tiān qù, miǎn de lǘ yán huà duǎn cháng
literal: clear · breeze · two · sleeves · toward · court · go, avoid · common · folk · talk · short · long
natural: with only a clean breeze in my two sleeves I go to court, so the people will have nothing to gossip about

meaning.en: Yu Qian's declaration of integrity: he brings no gifts to the capital, so no one can say anything against him.
meaning.zh: 于谦自表清廉：进京不带礼物，只带两袖清风，免得百姓议论。

examples.zh: 新任局长在就职讲话中说：“清风两袖朝天去，免得闾阎话短长。”
examples.en: In his inaugural speech the new bureau chief said, 'With only a clean breeze in my sleeves I go, so the people will have nothing to say'.

examples.zh: 廉政展览里写着于谦的“清风两袖朝天去，免得闾阎话短长”。
examples.en: The exhibition on clean government displayed Yu Qian's 'clean breeze in my two sleeves'.

story.en: Yu Qian (1398-1457), a Ming official who defended Beijing in 1449, wrote this poem when refusing to bring local specialities as gifts on his trips to the capital.
story.zh: 于谦（1398—1457）是明代大臣，1449年领导北京保卫战；他进京不肯携带土产送礼，作此诗明志。

usage.en: The source of 两袖清风. Quoted when praising honest officials. Formal and literary.
usage.zh: 成语“两袖清风”的出处，用来赞扬清廉的官员，正式、书面。

text: 但愿苍生俱饱暖，不辞辛苦出山林
pinyin: dàn yuàn cāng shēng jù bǎo nuǎn, bù cí xīn kǔ chū shān lín
literal: only · wish · common · people · all · fed · warm, not · decline · toil · leave · mountain · forest
natural: if only the common people could all be fed and warm, I would gladly endure hardship and leave the mountains

meaning.en: Written as if spoken by coal: it comes out of the mountains to give warmth, hoping that ordinary people will have food and heat.
meaning.zh: 借煤炭口吻写成：愿意不辞辛苦走出深山，只希望百姓都能温饱。

equivalents: I only wish everyone could be warm and fed
serving the people at any cost

examples.zh: 这位老干部常说“但愿苍生俱饱暖，不辞辛苦出山林”。
examples.en: The veteran official often said 'if only the common people could all be fed and warm, I would gladly endure hardship'.

examples.zh: 志愿者们的信念就是“但愿苍生俱饱暖，不辞辛苦出山林”。
examples.en: The volunteers' creed is 'if only the people could all be fed and warm, I would gladly endure hardship'.

story.en: Attributed to Yu Qian (1398-1457), a poem in which coal speaks for the ideal of serving ordinary people.
story.zh: 传为于谦（1398—1457）所作，借煤炭抒发为百姓谋福的理想。

usage.en: Quoted for selfless public service and care for the people's livelihood. Literary.
usage.zh: 用来赞扬为民服务、关心民生，书面语。

text: 无善无恶心之体，有善有恶意之动；知善知恶是良知，为善去恶是格物
pinyin: wú shàn wú è xīn zhī tǐ, yǒu shàn yǒu è yì zhī dòng, zhī shàn zhī è shì liáng zhī, wéi shàn qù è shì gé wù
literal: no · good · no · evil · mind · 's · substance, have · good · have · evil · intention · 's · stirring, know · good · know · evil · is · innate · knowing, do · good · remove · evil · is · investigating · things
natural: the mind in itself is neither good nor evil; good and evil arise when intention stirs; knowing good from evil is innate knowing, and doing good and removing evil is investigating things

meaning.en: Wang Yangming's 'Four-Sentence Teaching', the core of his philosophy: the mind is originally neutral, intention gives rise to good and evil, conscience tells them apart, and self-cultivation is acting on it.
meaning.zh: 王阳明的“四句教”，概括其心学要旨：心体本来无善无恶，意念一动才有善恶，良知能分辨善恶，修养功夫就是为善去恶。

examples.zh: 课上讲王阳明时，老师把“无善无恶心之体，有善有恶意之动；知善知恶是良知，为善去恶是格物”写在了黑板上。
examples.en: When lecturing on Wang Yangming the teacher wrote his Four-Sentence Teaching on the board.

examples.zh: 读书会的话题是“无善无恶心之体，有善有恶意之动；知善知恶是良知，为善去恶是格物”。
examples.en: The reading group's topic was the Four-Sentence Teaching: 'the mind in itself is neither good nor evil ...'.

story.en: Wang Yangming (1472-1529) stated this teaching in 1527 before setting out on his last campaign, in the 'Tianquan' exchange with his disciples Qian Dehong and Wang Ji; it is recorded in the 《传习录》 and his chronological biography.
story.zh: 王阳明（1472—1529）于1527年出征广西前，在天泉桥与弟子钱德洪、王畿论学时提出此说，见《传习录》及年谱。

usage.en: Quoted in discussions of Neo-Confucian and Yangming thought; interpretations of the first line are much debated. Philosophical and literary.
usage.zh: 谈论宋明理学与阳明心学时引用，对第一句的解释争议很大。哲学性、书面语。

text: 你未看此花时，此花与汝心同归于寂
pinyin: nǐ wèi kàn cǐ huā shí, cǐ huā yǔ rǔ xīn tóng guī yú jì
literal: you · not yet · look · this · flower · time, this · flower · with · your · mind · together · return · to · stillness
natural: before you looked at this flower, it and your mind were alike in silence

meaning.en: Wang Yangming's reply to a friend who asked whether flowers on a mountain exist apart from the mind: unseen, a flower is in stillness with the mind, and only on being seen does its colour appear.
meaning.zh: 王阳明回答友人“山中花树自开自落与我心何关”：你没看这花时，花与你的心同样沉寂，看到时花的颜色才明白起来。

equivalents: a flower unseen is a flower unknown

examples.zh: 哲学课上讨论“你未看此花时，此花与汝心同归于寂”，同学们争论不休。
examples.en: In philosophy class students argued endlessly over 'before you looked at this flower, it and your mind were alike in silence'.

examples.zh: 他在读书笔记里抄下“你未看此花时，此花与汝心同归于寂”。
examples.en: In his reading notes he copied out 'before you looked at this flower, it and your mind were alike in silence'.

story.en: In the 《传习录》 a friend points to flowering trees in the mountains and asks what they have to do with his mind; Wang answers with this line and continues, 你来看此花时，则此花颜色一时明白起来.
story.zh: 《传习录》下卷记载，友人指着岩中花树问其与心有何关系，王阳明以此答之，并接着说“你来看此花时，则此花颜色一时明白起来”。

usage.en: Often cited to illustrate Wang Yangming's idealist thought; it is sometimes read as subjective idealism, though scholars interpret it differently. Philosophical.
usage.zh: 常用来说明王阳明的心学观点，有人视作主观唯心论，学界理解不一。哲学性用语。

text: 桃花坞里桃花庵，桃花庵里桃花仙
pinyin: táo huā wù lǐ táo huā ān, táo huā ān lǐ táo huā xiān
literal: peach · blossom · hollow (Taohuawu, a place in Suzhou) · in · peach · blossom · hermitage, peach · blossom · hermitage · in · peach · blossom · immortal
natural: in Peach Blossom Dock stands the Peach Blossom Hermitage, and in the hermitage lives a peach-blossom immortal

meaning.en: The opening of Tang Yin's song, a playful, repetitive self-portrait: the poet as a carefree peach-blossom immortal in his own retreat.
meaning.zh: 唐寅《桃花庵歌》开篇，以回环往复的句式自画像：他是隐居桃花庵中的逍遥桃花仙。

equivalents: living like an immortal among the blossoms

examples.zh: 民宿的门口挂着“桃花坞里桃花庵，桃花庵里桃花仙”。
examples.en: At the entrance of the guesthouse hung 'in Peach Blossom Dock stands the Peach Blossom Hermitage'.

examples.zh: 他把新买的小院取名桃花庵，还抄上“桃花坞里桃花庵，桃花庵里桃花仙”。
examples.en: He named his newly bought little courtyard the Peach Blossom Hermitage and copied the line out for it.

story.en: Tang Yin (1470-1524), a painter-poet of Suzhou, built a retreat at Peach Blossom Dock after failing in the civil service examination scandal of 1499.
story.zh: 唐寅（1470—1524）是苏州的画家兼诗人，1499年卷入科场案后，在桃花坞建屋隐居。

usage.en: Loved for its playful rhythm and often used for rural retreats or romantic recluse images. Literary.
usage.zh: 因回环有趣的节奏而深受喜爱，常用于田园隐居的意象，书面语。

text: 酒醒只在花前坐，酒醉还来花下眠
pinyin: jiǔ xǐng zhǐ zài huā qián zuò, jiǔ zuì hái lái huā xià mián
literal: wine · sober · only · at · flower · front · sit, wine · drunk · still · come · flower · under · sleep
natural: when sober I only sit before the flowers; when drunk I come back to sleep beneath them

meaning.en: A line from Tang Yin's song: his days are spent between wine and blossoms, without ambition for office.
meaning.zh: 唐寅《桃花庵歌》中的诗句：日子只在酒与花之间，不求仕进。

examples.zh: 退休后的老张整天养花喝茶，说自己是“酒醒只在花前坐，酒醉还来花下眠”。
examples.en: Retired, Old Zhang spends his days with flowers and tea and says he is 'sober, I sit by the flowers; drunk, I sleep beneath them'.

examples.zh: 春天的公园里，有人铺着毯子，真像“酒醒只在花前坐，酒醉还来花下眠”。
examples.en: In the park in spring, people lay out blankets, just like 'when drunk I come back to sleep beneath the flowers'.

story.en: One of the best-known couplets of Tang Yin's 《桃花庵歌》, written in his retirement at Suzhou.
story.zh: 唐寅在苏州隐居期间所作《桃花庵歌》中最有名的诗句之一。

usage.en: Quoted for a leisurely, wine-and-flowers life. Literary and often playful.
usage.zh: 形容闲散、饮酒赏花的生活，书面语，常带戏谑。

text: 但愿老死花酒间，不愿鞠躬车马前
pinyin: dàn yuàn lǎo sǐ huā jiǔ jiān, bù yuàn jū gōng chē mǎ qián
literal: only · wish · grow old · die · flowers · wine · among, not · wish · bow · carriage · horse · before
natural: I would rather grow old and die among flowers and wine than bow before carriages and horses

meaning.en: Tang Yin's choice of a free, modest life over bowing and scraping to the rich and powerful.
meaning.zh: 唐寅宁愿自由闲散地终老，也不愿向权贵卑躬屈膝。

equivalents: I'd rather live free than grovel
refusing to bow to the powerful

examples.zh: 他辞掉工作开了间花店，常说“但愿老死花酒间，不愿鞠躬车马前”。
examples.en: He quit his job to open a flower shop, often saying 'I would rather die among flowers and wine than bow before carriages and horses'.

examples.zh: 面对权贵的邀请，他笑着回了句“但愿老死花酒间，不愿鞠躬车马前”。
examples.en: Faced with an invitation from the powerful, he replied with a smile, 'I would rather die among flowers and wine than bow before carriages and horses'.

story.en: The song also has the lines 'compare wealth with poverty: one is on the plain, one in heaven; compare poverty with carriages and horses: they must hurry, I have leisure', which make the same choice.
story.zh: 《桃花庵歌》后文又说“若将富贵比贫贱，一在平地一在天；若将贫贱比车马，他得驱驰我得闲”，表明同样的选择。

usage.en: Quoted by those who prefer freedom to career advancement; the tone is proud, and can be self-mocking. 车马 stands for the rich and powerful.
usage.zh: 用于表示宁愿自由也不要仕途，语气清高，也可自嘲。“车马”借指权贵。

text: 原来姹紫嫣红开遍，似这般都付与断井颓垣
pinyin: yuán lái chà zǐ yān hóng kāi biàn, sì zhè bān dōu fù yǔ duàn jǐng tuí yuán
literal: so · it · turns · out · deep · purple · tender · red · open · everywhere, like · this · sort · all · given · to · broken · well · fallen · wall
natural: so the dazzling purples and reds bloom everywhere, only to be left to broken wells and crumbling walls

meaning.en: Du Liniang's lament in 'The Peony Pavilion': the garden's splendour is blooming unseen and will be lost, just as her own youth is passing.
meaning.zh: 《牡丹亭》中杜丽娘的唱词：满园繁花盛开却无人欣赏，终将落在残垣断井之间，一如她自己的青春。

equivalents: all that glory left to ruin

examples.zh: 看完昆曲《游园惊梦》，她久久回味着“原来姹紫嫣红开遍，似这般都付与断井颓垣”。
examples.en: After watching the Kunqu scene 'Strolling in the Garden', she lingered over 'so the dazzling purples and reds bloom everywhere ...'.

examples.zh: 老街拆迁前，他想起“原来姹紫嫣红开遍，似这般都付与断井颓垣”，心里一阵惆怅。
examples.en: Before the old street was demolished he thought of 'dazzling purples and reds bloom everywhere, only for broken wells and crumbling walls', and felt wistful.

story.en: Tang Xianzu (1550-1616) completed 《牡丹亭》 in 1598; the line is sung by Du Liniang when she wanders into her family's garden and sees it neglected.
story.zh: 汤显祖（1550—1616）于1598年完成《牡丹亭》；此句是杜丽娘游园时见满园荒废所唱。

usage.en: Quoted for splendour passing unnoticed, and for the sorrow of youth wasted. Literary, from a sung opera aria (the 皂罗袍 tune). 姹紫嫣红 and 断井颓垣 also exist as idioms of their own.
usage.zh: 用来感叹美景无人欣赏、青春虚度，书面语，出自昆曲唱段（【皂罗袍】）。“姹紫嫣红”“断井颓垣”也各自是成语。

text: 雾凇沆砀，天与云与山与水，上下一白
pinyin: wù sōng hàng dàng, tiān yǔ yún yǔ shān yǔ shuǐ, shàng xià yī bái
literal: rime · mist · vast, sky · and · cloud · and · mountain · and · water, above · below · one · white
natural: rime and mist spread vast; sky, cloud, mountain and water, above and below, all one white

meaning.en: Zhang Dai's description of West Lake after a heavy snow: everything merges into a single whiteness.
meaning.zh: 张岱描写大雪后的西湖：天、云、山、水融成一片白色。

examples.zh: 清晨推开窗，“雾凇沆砀，天与云与山与水，上下一白”，正是张岱笔下的雪景。
examples.en: Opening the window in the morning, the scene was just as Zhang Dai wrote: 'rime and mist spread vast, above and below all one white'.

examples.zh: 作文里他引用了“雾凇沆砀，天与云与山与水，上下一白”来写雪后的湖面。
examples.en: In his essay he quoted 'rime and mist spread vast ... all one white' to describe the lake after the snow.

origin.source: 张岱《陶庵梦忆·湖心亭看雪》

story.en: Zhang Dai (1597-c. 1679) recalls in 《湖心亭看雪》 a visit to the mid-lake pavilion on West Lake during a snowfall in 1632, written after the fall of the Ming.
story.zh: 张岱（1597—约1679）在《湖心亭看雪》中追记1632年大雪时到西湖湖心亭看雪的情景，文章写于明亡之后。

date.en: late Ming to early Qing, mid-17th c.

usage.en: A classic of descriptive prose, often quoted for snow scenes. 沆砀 means a vast, hazy expanse of mist. Literary.
usage.zh: 描写雪景的经典文句。“沆砀”形容白气弥漫的样子，书面语。

text: 人无癖不可与交，以其无深情也；人无疵不可与交，以其无真气也
pinyin: rén wú pǐ bù kě yǔ jiāo, yǐ qí wú shēn qíng yě, rén wú cī bù kě yǔ jiāo, yǐ qí wú zhēn qì yě
literal: person · lack · obsession · not · may · with · befriend, because · he · lacks · deep · feeling · indeed, person · lack · flaw · not · may · with · befriend, because · he · lacks · true · spirit · indeed
natural: do not befriend someone with no obsession, for he has no deep feeling; do not befriend someone with no flaws, for he has no real spirit

meaning.en: Zhang Dai's view of friendship: people who have a passion or a flaw show genuine feeling and character.
meaning.zh: 张岱的交友观：有癖好、有缺点的人才有真情实感。

examples.zh: 张岱说“人无癖不可与交，以其无深情也；人无疵不可与交，以其无真气也”，所以他喜欢和有怪脾气的人做朋友。
examples.en: Zhang Dai said that one should not befriend those with no obsession or flaw, for they lack deep feeling and true spirit, so he liked making friends with eccentrics.

examples.zh: 同事爱收集旧钟表，我想起“人无癖不可与交，以其无深情也；人无疵不可与交，以其无真气也”。
examples.en: My colleague loves collecting old clocks, which reminds me of Zhang Dai's remark that people with no obsession or flaw lack deep feeling and true spirit.

origin.source: 张岱《陶庵梦忆·祁止祥癖》

story.en: In 《祁止祥癖》 Zhang Dai describes his friend Qi Zhixiang, whose passionate attachments he describes, and uses this reasoning to argue that such obsessions show genuine feeling.
story.zh: 张岱在《祁止祥癖》中写友人祁止祥的种种痴癖，并借此议论说明癖好正是真性情的表现。

date.en: late Ming to early Qing, mid-17th c.

usage.en: Often quoted to justify quirks and hobbies, or to praise an eccentric friend. Literary. 癖 means a passion or craze, 疵 a flaw.
usage.zh: 常用来为个人癖好辩护，或夸赞有个性的朋友，书面语。“癖”指嗜好，“疵”指缺点。

text: 封侯非我意，但愿海波平
pinyin: fēng hóu fēi wǒ yì, dàn yuàn hǎi bō píng
literal: be · enfeoffed · marquis · not · my · wish, only · wish · sea · waves · calm
natural: becoming a marquis is not what I want; I only wish for calm seas

meaning.en: Qi Jiguang's declaration: he fights the pirates not for rank or title but for peace along the coast.
meaning.zh: 戚继光自述心志：抗倭不为封侯拜爵，只愿海疆平静。

equivalents: peace, not glory, is the goal
I serve for safety, not honours

examples.zh: 毕业时他选择去边防工作，说自己“封侯非我意，但愿海波平”。
examples.en: On graduating he chose to work on border defence, saying 'becoming a marquis is not what I want; I only wish for calm seas'.

examples.zh: 海警学院的新生宣誓后，教官引用“封侯非我意，但愿海波平”。
examples.en: After the new cadets' oath at the coast guard academy the instructor quoted 'I only wish for calm seas'.

story.en: Qi Jiguang (1528-1588), the Ming general who fought the wokou pirates, wrote this couplet in the poem 《韬钤深处》, which also contains 十年驱驰海色寒.
story.zh: 戚继光（1528—1588）是抗倭名将，此联出自其诗《韬钤深处》，诗中另有“十年驱驰海色寒”。

usage.en: Quoted for selfless service in the military and the coast guard. Formal and literary.
usage.zh: 用于军人、海防人员等无私奉献的场合，正式、书面。

text: 以天下之利尽归于己，以天下之害尽归于人
pinyin: yǐ tiān xià zhī lì jìn guī yú jǐ, yǐ tiān xià zhī hài jìn guī yú rén
literal: take · world · 's · benefit · all · return · to · self, take · world · 's · harm · all · return · to · others
natural: taking all the world's benefits for oneself and leaving all its harms to others

meaning.en: Huang Zongxi's description of a self-serving ruler: he keeps every advantage of the realm for himself and passes every burden to the people.
meaning.zh: 黄宗羲对自私君主的描述：把天下所有好处据为己有，把所有祸害推给百姓。

equivalents: keep the gains, pass on the pain

examples.zh: 评论员用“以天下之利尽归于己，以天下之害尽归于人”批评这种垄断行为。
examples.en: The commentator used 'taking all the world's benefits for oneself and leaving the harms to others' to criticise such monopolistic behaviour.

examples.zh: 他在读书笔记中摘抄了“以天下之利尽归于己，以天下之害尽归于人”。
examples.en: In his reading notes he copied out 'taking all the world's benefits for oneself and leaving the harms to others'.

origin.source: 黄宗羲《明夷待访录·原君》

story.en: From the chapter 《原君》 ('On the Ruler') in Huang Zongxi's 《明夷待访录》, in which he argues that later rulers made the realm their private property.
story.zh: 出自黄宗羲《明夷待访录·原君》，他认为后世君主把天下变成了自己的私产。

usage.en: Used to criticise selfish rulers or powerful groups that keep the gains and push the costs onto others. Formal.
usage.zh: 批评自私的统治者或权势集团独占好处、转嫁损失，正式用语。
